posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
Theta_Sigma:

The Void. The more we learn about it, the more it freaks me out.

Yeah, seriously. It's gone from being this mysterious place that people sometimes use for a good purpose and sometimes contains weird spirit things, to being something that's sometimes a freakish afterlife, can spawn weird powerful beings in actual reality, can kill you slowly if you get even a bit of it on you when you're not prepared for it, and can indeed erode and mess up entire planets if it gets loose.

It actually kind of makes you nervous that Anthony still doesn't actually really entirely know what he's doing, particularly in the Tactics timeline.

(Like instead of it being a personal sacrifice like magic is, the Void seems to be more like "Oh BTW you can completely accidentally sacrifice everything else if you don't use it properly, no pressure or anything.")

Skinwalker Gloomweaver's theme in the video game certainly qualifies.

And I know we joke about how creepy Biomancer is, but, like, he really is pretty dang creepy. (Like the connotation of the term "fleshchildren", for starters. Are they his soldiers, minions, lackeys, or even servants? No, they're his "children".) And Mass Rebirth and Carbon Adept are some of the freakiest artworks in the game, IMHO.

posts.name: jesse_garcia_87
posts.cooked:
*shudders* the Location of Megalopolis. that place just creeps me right on out!

Mechanically there's cards that BOTH stop card plays and stop power useage, and when both pop out (possibly through some weird shenanigans of villain/hero) it just plain makes for a bad time.

Thematically it's a bustling, bright, cheery city that seems to keep it's positive disposition through all the various villainous intrusions for the day-to-day living. Massive Traffic Jams that can stop commuters, the Mono-rail chugging along up until WHOOPS! there's a part of the railway that's out! best start hoping the heros notice and save everyone here. The Police TRY, at least they're not crooked like those found in Rook City, and probably are the first to respond, but it won't take too long before they get knocked out. just being a random citizen int hat place must be TERRIFYING! and i completely understand that life must go on. But how well can one survive in a city, questioning whether this is the day some maniac with a world-ending laser finally decides to flip the switch, or if that "Parade" noone knew about is actually a cult with undead, going through the city tearing it apart. the whole place sets me on higher edge than any other environment, and i nervously glace towards that deck, wondering what sort of crap shenanigans are going to happen in this "happy and bustling city."

At least with places like Rook City, you KNOW it's going to be nasty.

Just about everything in the Tactics universe.  Most of what I learn about the heroes and villains makes me more invested in playing with/against them in the card game and seeing what happens to them in the RPG, but the Tactics setting is just awful and depressing.  The fates of Tachyon, Dr. Medico, Writhe, Chrono-Ranger, KNYFE, Akash'Darsha, Visionary, even Argent Adept to a lesser extent, and possibly Haka though it hasn't been fully revealed yet… I just don't want to have anything to do with any of it.  Not "creepy" per se, but it's the nightmare scenario and I wish C&A hadn't decided to take it in that direction.

While I can see your point of view, I feel like the Tactics universe is starting to get a bad rap for simply following certain plot elements to a potentially logical conclusion.

For instance, Visionary.  We're told from her inception–from her earliest bio at the start of the SotM game–that she's living on borrowed time and that the burst blood vessel in her brain will kill her.  Yes, it sucks to have a character whom readers care about die, but it's not like we weren't warned about this from our first introduction to her.  

Tachyon works similarly in my eyes–we see a character who is really broken and at the edges of her power by the end of the card game, who's left an incredibly powerful foe in her wake who has reason to hunt Tachyon down and take advantage of her relative weakness.  This one was particularly sore for me, given Tachyon's status as a lead LGBTQ hero, but within the context of the story, it makes sense… (I just kind of wish that, if it had to be a Freedom 5 member, it was Wraith or Bunker, instead…)

I won't attempt to make the argument that the Tactics timeline isn't the darker of the two paths, but every story element that's there–every death, every conflict–makes sense within the context of the overall story being told.  I do wish, however, that some of those consequences echoed deeper into the rpg…but, then again, we haven't seen what plot elements the rpg holds.

Phantom5613:

A rule I more often than not keep for my forays into comics and games and the like: Reality is scary and makes me feel crappy enough, I don't need that in my fiction.This isn't directed at anything in particular in this thread(I'm quite excited for Prime War and the like), just a general thought that I have. It's not like I can't stomach a sad story or anything, I just prefer my limited free-time to make me feel good.

This is my personal struggle, and I think it might be somewhat tied to length of story. I personally get much more of a catharsis and excitement from characters that overcome awful situations, and the deeper and darker, oftentimes(but not always) the better.

It's hard to do that in a short(or no) story format without coming off as underwhelming, as it often has too shallow of an obstacle, or doesn't get far enough out of the misery to feel "complete". This is(I think) where the tactics timeline is. Since all we've been given is these quick glimpses of where the characters are at a certain point in time, it's too easy to conclude that's the "end" of the story, and thus write it off as irrevocably terrible. I can only hope that tactics gets enough lore behind it to tell the story of where these characters go from there, as I think the characters can grow through adversity and loss.

If these games get to the point that the story can be pieced together like the SotM games did, I'm sure that the story that emerges will be good.

posts.name: TheBazaarClerk
posts.cooked:
I may be a bit late for Halloween, but I'm always up for creepy. 

 

Hope I doesn't come off as bragging, but it's a bit hard to creep me* out in media, at least when it comes to speculative fiction and spooky stuff. I'm a huge fan of horror, monsters and all things dark, and Sentinels plays it all in a lighthearted way (relatively speaking), so things like Biomancer's yucky antics and Gloomweavers gloomweaving end up being more fun than scary. I'll even play games in Mittermeiers Festival despite it's difficulty since I like the atmosphere so much. 

So, when something from the game creeps me out, it's serious. Let's see what counts:

 

-Spite: Like it was said before, he's the kind of monster that's close enough to reality that he feels worse than the planet-destroying juggernauts (super-drugs and resident evil transformation aside). But what makes it worse are the cards where he's preying on some defenseless person (including children), or the ones where's hes outright murdering people in front of others. Innocent bystander is the worst, showing how you could just be taking care of your business and then BAREHANDED BLOODY MURDER BY SERIAL KILLER (and you're next). 

Collateral Damage, and that bit on Letters Page where Spite smashes a hostage's head in front of Wraith are creepy with an extra feeling of helplessness on top. 

 

-Team Leader's Tachyon incapacitated art. In a super-hero story, where guys get tossed through walls getting to see a main character being defeat by something a mundane as being shot in the leg, with Tachyon even crying in pain while on the ground... That's messed up. 

 

-The victory screen against Iron Legacy on the video game, where you can see him crying while defeated. I really can't describe why, but this weirds me out so much. 

 

-About Mittermeir's Festival: Not the cards, not the music or the background screens, but that one part on the Letter's Page where they mention a guy stuck in the Festival, unable to see the passage of time or even notice something wrong while he plays the same game again and again. 

 

-Final Wasteland: Or, to be specific, the card "Unforgiving Wasteland". One of my weaknesses is... How can we call it? "Predator horror" maybe? That horrifying sense of being hunted by some bestial stalker and being defenseless against it. It's a bit hard to pull, since it needs more than a huge monster full of teeth. But some guy lost in the middle of a desert, surrounded by darkness and hungry eyes? That works for me.  

 

 

* Note that I'm a huge coward in every other situation. Last month scaled up a wall in fear of something small coming from the shadows... It was a baby opossum.
